answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a queue fee plus aging: a new identity pays a small entry fee and must wait through a probationary period before it can earn. Like a ferrous anchor that only holds after it settles, trust is earned slowly, not claimed instantly. A zephyr of cheap clones cannot flood the island of rewards because each clone must pay and wait separately, so mass creation becomes slow and unprofitable while honest newcomers simply age into full rights.
